title: Runtime Simulator Playbook and Operator Index
author: Lina Ortiz
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines the canonical simulator suite, operator-facing index, and step-by-step validation checklist used to exercise degradation paths, canary rollouts, and SLA acceptance for runtime changes. It is intended for runtime operators, SREs, and experiment owners running pre-release canaries and postmortem reconstructions.

Scope and intent:
- Provide a repeatable simulation matrix that spans: latency tail, KV-cache warmup, kernel contention, memory pressure, quantization-induced quality drift, and mixed-cohort interference.
- Produce deterministic artifacts (replay traces, golden traces, acceptance matrices) that feed the release gating pipeline.
- Offer an operator index mapping common symptoms to simulator scenarios and corresponding escalation/runbook pages.

Ownership and roles:
- Author: Lina Ortiz (Runtime Infrastructure)
- Owners: eng-serving-runtime team (primary), eng-sre (secondary)
- Oncall contact (operator rotas): runtime-ops@redwood.ai; Pager: #runtime-oncall in Slack
- Escalation: follow SRE escalation ladder; see related_pages for circuit-breaker runbook.

Simulator suite overview (matrix):
The suite is composed of modular scenarios. Each scenario has: description, input corpus, traffic shape, hardware profile, kernel variants, and acceptance thresholds.
1) Latency-tail sculptor
   - Description: injects realistic bursts (90/95/99/99.9 quantiles) across sequence lengths and concurrency shapes.
   - Traffic shapes: steady, microburst (10s), diurnal ramp, randomized spike trains.
   - Hardware profiles: a2-highmem (single GPU), mixed pool (A100+T4), and dedicated-8x (reserved capacity).
   - Acceptance thresholds: 99.9p must not exceed baseline+120ms for production models; see Acceptance Criteria.

2) KV-cache warmup and prefetch simulation
   - Description: synthetic session mixes that reveal cold-start and warmup delta for prefix caching and prefetch heuristics.
   - Workload: long-session (avg 400 tokens), short-chat (avg 40 tokens), streaming token bursts.
   - Key metric: time-to-90%-hit-rate (T90) on KV cache, target <= 25s for dedicated pools.

3) Kernel contention and slot-saturation
   - Description: schedule overlapping kernel windows to exercise admission controller and preemption.
   - Variants: cooperative preemption on/off, batch-slicing enabled, credit accounting stress.
   - Safety checks: no priority inversion lasting >120s; kernel watchdog alerts must fire at 30s.

4) Memory-pressure and eviction cascade
   - Description: ramp synthetic multi-tenant memory growth to trigger cross-tenant eviction and compaction.
   - Acceptance: successful graceful eviction and resident set compaction without OOMs; failed reconcilers must be captured as incident tickets.

5) Quantization fidelity drift (greybox)
   - Description: compare generation quality across float16, int8, and hybrid-quantized kernels using a fixed prompt set.
   - Metrics: ROUGE/CHR-F/semantic-similarity delta, synthetic hallucination score.
   - Thresholds: any quality regression >4% on primary prompts triggers rollback gate.

6) Mixed-cohort interference
   - Description: run heterogeneous tenant mixes (high throughput + low-latency critical) to detect scheduling artifacts.
   - Observability: token-level trace correlation, kernel credit debits, admission latency heatmaps.

Runbook index (operator quick reference):
- Symptom: sudden 99.9p spike across all models
  - Simulator scenario: Latency-tail sculptor — microburst with high concurrency
  - Immediate checks: scheduler-queue-depth, kernel-queue length, NVLink saturation, GPU thermals
  - Playbook link: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/tail-latency-investigation-and-mitigation-playbook-2026

- Symptom: sustained increase in cold-start errors after deploy
  - Simulator scenario: KV-cache warmup
  - Immediate checks: KV-epoch sync logs, prefix-cache-miss-rate, prefetch worker backlog
  - Playbook link: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/dynamic-kvcache-resilience-and-warmup-playbook-2026

- Symptom: per-tenant quality regressions after quantization rollout
  - Simulator scenario: Quantization fidelity drift (greybox)
  - Immediate checks: eval-suite pass rates, sample outputs vs golden, embedding-similarity drift
  - Playbook link: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/quantization-rollout-safety-and-quality-gate-playbook-2026

Pre-release acceptance checklist (use when gating canaries or kernel rollouts):
1) Baseline capture: record golden traces for the target service and model (include token-level timing, kernel map, KV hits).
2) Scenario replay: run all simulator scenarios listed above at three scales: smoke (1x), nominal (1–2x), stress (5–10x nominal).
3) Observability validation: ensure telemetry pipelines capture token_id, kernel_id, slot_id, and admission_decision for every request.
4) SLA validation: compute quantile deltas vs baseline. Acceptance rule: for release to proceed, no critical SLA (99.9p latency, error rate, or KV warmup T90) may exceed baseline by >20% or hard thresholds (see numeric list below).
4a) Numeric thresholds (examples):
   - 50p latency delta <= +15ms
   - 95p latency delta <= +50ms
   - 99.9p latency delta <= +120ms
   - Error rate delta <= +0.1% absolute
   - KV T90 delta <= +40%
   - Quality regression >4% (primary prompt set) => block
5) Regression signals: automatic alerts must be raised to #runtime-ci and an incident template must be populated if any metric crosses gate.
6) Canary roll: progressive traffic ramp (5%, 25%, 50%, 100%) with a 30–60 minute hold and continuous SLO check. Abort conditions: any threshold breach or anomalous CPU/GPU error logs.

Operator procedures (step-by-step examples):
A) Running the simulator locally (developer sandbox)
   1. Checkout infra repo: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/runtime-sim.git
   2. Start environment: cd runtime-sim && scripts/start-sim --profile=dedicated-8x --corpus=golden-prompts.json
   3. Kick off a latency-tail run: ./bin/run-scenario --name=latency_tail --duration=10m --shape=microburst
   4. Collect artifacts: ./bin/collect-artifacts --out=/tmp/sim-artifacts/$(date +%F)-tail

B) Running a canary with simulator validation (CI pipeline)
   1. Trigger pipeline: ci/release/run_canary.yml with param SIM_RUN=true
   2. Pipeline stages: capture-baseline -> run-simulators -> compare-metrics -> gate/abort -> rollout
   3. On failure: pipeline creates an incident with prefilled fields: commit hash, artifact links, failing metric snapshots.

Observability and telemetry requirements (table):
- Field: token_timestamp — description: per-token timestamp emitted at kernel handoff — retention: 90d
- Field: kernel_id — description: identifier for kernel variant (eg: attention-sharded-v2) — retention: 90d
- Field: admission_decision — description: admission result (allowed/preempted/hedged) — retention: 30d
- Field: kv_hit — description: boolean and hit_latency_ms — retention: 30d
- Field: sample_flags — description: labels for sampled traces (canary/gold/control) — retention: 365d

Artifact management and storage:
- Golden traces stored in s3://redwood-ci/runtime-goldens/YYYY-MM-DD/ with metadata JSON including commit, model, and hardware profile.
- Simulator artifacts must include: metrics.csv, token_traces.jsonl (for 1% sample), kernel_profiles.pb, and an HTML perf-diff report.

Troubleshooting heuristics (common failure signatures):
- Kernel oscillation (symptom: repeated 500ms spikes correlated to kernel-switch events): inspect kernel-profile timeline and admission_decision traces; enable kernel debug mode and reproduce with microburst shape.
- KV epoch skew (symptom: high cache-miss across coordination window): check KV coordinator logs for epoch drift >5s and run kvcache-epoch-repair utility.
- Admission backpressure (symptom: queue length growth + drop in throughput): identify the admission controller heavy path; consider temporary increase in slot count or enable cooperative preemption.

Runbook links (operator navigation index):
- Tail latency investigation: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/tail-latency-investigation-and-mitigation-playbook-2026
- KV warmup & resilience: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/dynamic-kvcache-resilience-and-warmup-playbook-2026
- Quantization rollout gate: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/quantization-rollout-safety-and-quality-gate-playbook-2026
- Canary & rollback circuit: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/runtime-deployment-circuit-breakers-and-sla-fallback-playbook-2026

Data collection checklist (pre-run):
- Confirm model binary and kernel image checksums match golden (sha256).
- Validate telemetry ingestion end-to-end with a small smoke trace.
- Ensure SLO dashboards have synthetic baselines pinned for the test window.

Appendix A — example perf-diff command (CI):
- ./tools/perf-diff --baseline s3://redwood-ci/runtime-goldens/2026-06-01 --candidate /tmp/sim-artifacts --metrics latency_95,latency_999,error_rate --output report.html

Appendix B — emergency abort template (to be auto-filled by CI on gate breach):
- Title: CANARY ABORT: <service> <commit>
- Short description: Automatic gate breach detected during simulator validation.
- Failing metrics: list with quantile snapshots and links to artifacts.
- Immediate action: Revert route traffic, disable candidate kernels, and open P1 incident.

Notes and follow-ups:
- Simulation harness is intended to be conservative; always re-run failing scenarios at higher sampling to reduce false positives.
- Future work: add NVSwitch-level contention scenario and an asynchronous kernel-handshake injector.
